description: Using spreadsheets to organise, analyse and model data: structured tables, formulas and references, lookup and logical functions, pivot tables, charts, descriptive statistics, what-if analysis with goal seek and Solver, and building a sound business model. Every skill is practised on real-looking local datasets in a spreadsheet that runs in the browser, with each exercise checked automatically for correct formulas as well as correct answers.
modelledOn: Winston, Microsoft Excel Data Analysis and Business Modeling
Powell and Baker, Business Analytics: The Art of Modeling with Spreadsheets
Ragsdale, Spreadsheet Modeling and Decision Analysis
Microsoft Office Specialist: Excel Expert certification
outcomes: Organise raw data into clean, validated tables suitable for analysis.
Write correct formulas with relative, absolute and mixed references and use statistical, text, date, lookup and logical functions.
Summarise and explore data with conditional aggregation, pivot tables and descriptive statistics.
Choose and build charts and simple dashboards that communicate findings honestly.
Perform what-if analysis with data tables, scenarios, goal seek and Solver.
Build, document and check a small business model that separates inputs, calculations and outputs.

units.title: Organising data in tables
topics: Rows as records and columns as fields; one table per subject; avoiding merged cells and blank rows
Data types and formats: numbers, text, dates, currency in cedis and percentages
Structured tables and named ranges
Data validation with drop-down lists and input rules
Sorting, filtering, removing duplicates, text to columns and importing CSV files
Running dataset: a market trader's daily sales log

units.title: Formulas, references and functions
topics: Operators and precedence; relative, absolute and mixed references
Mathematical and statistical functions: SUM, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA, ROUND
Text functions: LEFT, RIGHT, MID, LEN, TRIM, PROPER, CONCAT, TEXTJOIN; cleaning phone numbers
Date and time functions: TODAY, DATE, EOMONTH, NETWORKDAYS, DATEDIF
Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE and SEQUENCE
Error values and formula auditing: trace precedents and dependents, evaluate formula

units.title: Lookup and logical functions
topics: IF, nested IF, IFS, AND, OR, NOT and IFERROR
Conditional aggregation: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS
VLOOKUP and HLOOKUP and their limitations; INDEX with MATCH; XLOOKUP
Approximate-match lookups for bands: mobile money fee tiers and income tax brackets
Combining lookups across sheets; building a price list and invoice

units.title: Pivot tables and summaries
topics: Creating pivot tables: rows, columns, values and filters
Summarising by sum, count, average and percentage of total; grouping dates and numbers
Calculated fields, slicers and timelines
Cross-tabulating district health data by region, month and condition
Refreshing pivots when the source data changes

units.title: Charts in spreadsheets
topics: Choosing a chart: column, bar, line, scatter, pie, histogram and box plot
Formatting axes, labels and titles; combination charts and secondary axes
Misleading charts: truncated axes, 3-D effects and cherry-picked ranges
Conditional formatting, data bars and sparklines
Building a one-page dashboard

units.title: Descriptive statistics and trends
topics: Measures of centre and spread: mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation, percentiles
Frequency distributions and histograms with FREQUENCY and COUNTIFS
Correlation and scatter plots; trendlines
Simple linear regression with SLOPE, INTERCEPT and LINEST; forecasting with FORECAST and moving averages
Analysing seasonal cocoa prices or rainfall

units.title: What-if analysis and goal seek
topics: One- and two-variable data tables; sensitivity analysis
Scenario manager: best, worst and expected cases
Goal seek: break-even volume and target price
Solver for optimisation: linear programming for product mix and delivery routes
Financial functions: PMT, FV, NPV and IRR; a loan amortisation schedule

units.title: Building a simple business model
topics: Model design: separating inputs, calculations and outputs; documenting assumptions
Revenue, costs, profit and loss and a monthly cash-flow forecast for a small business such as a chop bar or a cocoa cooperative
Error checks, consistency totals and spreadsheet risk; well-known spreadsheet errors and their costs
Protecting sheets and cells, version control and sharing models
Presenting results and recommendations to a non-technical owner
Capstone: a complete, checked business model with a short report

schedule.title: Structuring data in a sheet
schedule.exercise: Redesign a messy trader's notebook table into a clean one-table-per-subject layout and list every change you made and why.

tasks.title: Convert a table with merged cells and blank rows into one record per row and check the record count equals the original entries
Format a column of prices in cedis, a date column and a percentage column, and fix five cells stored as text
Turn a range into a structured table with named columns and a named range, then write three formulas using those names

schedule.title: Validation and importing
schedule.exercise: Build an input sheet for a market trader's daily sales with validated entries and write the rules in a short guide.

tasks.title: Add drop-down lists and a rule rejecting negative quantities to a sales sheet, and test with five bad entries
Import a CSV of 300 sales rows, split a combined name and phone column, remove duplicates and report the rows before and after
Build the running dataset for a trader's daily sales log with validation, then sort and filter to answer five questions about it

schedule.title: Formulas and functions
schedule.exercise: Explain why a formula copied down gives wrong totals when a reference is not locked, with one corrected example.

tasks.title: Build a multiplication table using one formula with mixed references and copy it across and down, checking three cells by hand
Use SUM, AVERAGE, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, COUNT, COUNTA and ROUND on a column of weekly sales and report the results with correct rounding
Clean 50 phone numbers with TRIM, LEFT, MID and CONCAT into +233 form, and build full names with TEXTJOIN

schedule.title: Dates, dynamic arrays and auditing
schedule.exercise: Audit a given workbook with five formula errors and write the cause and fix for each.

tasks.title: Compute due dates, working days and ages for 20 loan records using DATE, EOMONTH, NETWORKDAYS and DATEDIF
Use FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE and SEQUENCE to list the top five customers and the distinct products sold, with live updating
Find and fix errors such as #REF, #N/A and #DIV/0 in a workbook using trace precedents and evaluate formula, noting the cause of each

schedule.title: Logic and conditional summaries
schedule.exercise: Write the formulas and the expected results for a commission scheme using IFS, SUMIFS and a lookup.

tasks.title: Compute a grade and pass flag from marks using IF, IFS and AND, and handle blanks with IFERROR
Use SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS and MAXIFS to summarise sales by region, product and month
Look up prices with VLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH and XLOOKUP, and show a case where VLOOKUP breaks after a column is inserted

schedule.title: Lookups for bands and invoices
schedule.exercise: Build a tax calculator and a fee table for mobile money transfers and test it with edge amounts.

tasks.title: Find a mobile money fee from a tier table using an approximate-match lookup and test with amounts at each tier boundary
Compute income tax from a bracketed table using a lookup and a cumulative method and verify with three worked salaries
Build a price list and invoice that pulls prices and tax by product code across sheets and handles unknown codes with a clear message

schedule.title: Pivot tables
schedule.exercise: Produce a pivot summary of district health data and write three sentences saying what a manager should do about it.

tasks.title: Create a pivot table of sales by product and month and answer three questions from it
Summarise sales as sum, count and percent of total, and group dates by month and quarter and ages into bands
Cross-tabulate district health data by region, month and condition with slicers, refresh after adding new rows, and explain the changes

schedule.title: Charts and dashboards
schedule.exercise: Redraw two misleading charts honestly and explain what each original hid.

tasks.title: Choose and draw the right chart for six data questions and say why each alternative would mislead
Correct a truncated axis, 3-D pie and cherry-picked range in three charts and compare the impressions before and after
Build a one-page sales dashboard with four charts, slicers, conditional formatting and sparklines that all update from one table

schedule.title: Statistics and forecasting
schedule.exercise: Analyse a year of cocoa prices or rainfall, describe the trend and seasonal pattern, and give a forecast with its limits.

tasks.title: Compute the mean, median, mode, standard deviation and quartiles of 40 daily sales and describe the skew
Build a frequency table with FREQUENCY and COUNTIFS for 100 maize prices and draw the histogram
Fit a trend with SLOPE and INTERCEPT, check it with LINEST, and forecast three months of cocoa prices with a moving average for comparison

schedule.title: What-if analysis
schedule.exercise: Describe the best, worst and expected case for a small bakery and the decision each would trigger.

tasks.title: Build a one-variable data table showing profit at different prices and a two-variable table of price and volume
Set up a scenario manager with best, worst and expected cases for a bakery and compare the results in a summary
Use goal seek to find the break-even volume and the price giving a profit of 5000 cedis, and verify by hand

schedule.title: Optimisation and financial functions
schedule.exercise: Compare two loan offers using PMT, total interest and NPV and recommend one.

tasks.title: Build a loan schedule with PMT showing interest and principal each month and verify the final balance reaches zero
Use Solver to maximise profit for a product mix under labour and material limits and interpret the shadow prices

schedule.title: Financial models and spreadsheet risk
schedule.exercise: Document the assumptions of a chop bar model on one page and list five checks that would catch an error.

tasks.title: Reorganise a model into separate input, calculation and output sheets with an assumptions table and trace one result to its inputs
Build a monthly cash-flow forecast for a chop bar with revenue, costs and profit and loss, and test a 20 percent fall in sales

schedule.title: Protecting, presenting and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present your capstone model's key findings and recommendation to a non-technical owner in five minutes.

tasks.title: Protect formula cells, leave input cells open, add a version log and share the workbook so a colleague can change only inputs
Turn a model's results into a one-page summary chart and three plain-language recommendations for an owner
Build a complete business model for a small business with inputs, scenarios, error checks and dashboard, and pass a review checklist
